guard: an inline persona is validated and bounded like a file, written only after the grant, launched from its own snapshot, and removed with its seat; a saved copy keeps the checked grant
why: N1 opens the closed record. N2 lets another launch read a seat's snapshot. N3 lets a clash reach
allocation, so it refuses after the spawn started. N4 writes the catalog copy before the grant, so
a refused user-auth grant still leaves a reusable persona behind. N5 saves the record's omissions,
so a later spawner's own default fills the copy. N6 restarts a seat from a changed snapshot.
N7, N8 and N9 each drop one removal: the live slot free (the only one an open mesh has), the
static retirement terminal (the one a boot sweep reaches), and the spawn's own rollback (the only
one an open mesh's failed launch has). N10 lets a resume inventory point a seat at another file.
N11 keys the snapshot by the uid the spawn allocated, which a hosted enrollment replaces.
N12a and N12b each drop one half of the restart's path check, so each half has its own cell.
N13 lets a spawn whose snapshot write found a file at its path delete that file at the terminal.
N14 writes strings a YAML reader takes for an alias, a null or a number. N15 writes the record's
role and model where the spawn overrode them. N16 lets a failed removal throw out of the rollback
before the grant's teardown is scheduled. N17, N18 and N19 mark a snapshot settled after a
removal that failed, on the rollback, the slot free and the stop, so no terminal retries or
reports it. N20 removes through a linked .cotal/run/inline. N21 writes a defined persona's
capabilities without bounding them against the definer.
